goals: mechanistic: characterize how runoff generation (surface runoff vs sub-surface drainage, snowmelt timing) varies across the basin's elevation and soil heterogeneity above the gauge
validation: reproduce the daily streamflow hydrograph at the American River gauge and report NSE

model_choice.rationale: ELM single-column resolves per-location water partitioning and snow, the runoff-GENERATION half of the hydrograph. It cannot route or aggregate runoff to a gauged discharge.

feasibility.verdict: infeasible for the primary ask (NSE against daily gauge hydrograph); partial for runoff-generation characterization
answerable: soil control on runoff partitioning (QOVER vs QDRAI) at sampled columns
column-level snowmelt/runoff generation behavior across strata
relative differences in water partitioning between elevation/soil groups

not_answerable.aspect: routed daily discharge at the American River gauge and its NSE
not_answerable.why: single-column ELM has no river routing and no mechanism to aggregate contributing-area runoff to a point hydrograph
not_answerable.needs: runoff routing / spatial aggregation over the contributing area above the gauge

not_answerable.aspect: elevation control on snow-driven hydrograph timing (the dominant control here)
not_answerable.why: forcing archive is uniform with no elevation downscaling; a column set stratified by elevation under uniform forcing varies by soil, not by the T/precip/snow gradient
requires spin-up to equilibrate soil moisture/snow storage before the comparison period

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation bands x dominant soils) over the contributing area above the gauge
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 elevation bands x 2 dominant soil classes = 6 columns spans the runoff-generation heterogeneity of the contributing area. Without routing, additional columns cannot improve a gauge hydrograph, so N is kept minimal and diagnostic.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate columns to span the rain-snow transition (mid band) where melt timing is most sensitive, and include valley footslopes where drainage/recharge partitioning differs. Placement restricted to the drainage area upstream of the American River gauge.
sampling_strategy.replication: None — each stratum cell sampled once; replication is not informative without routing to compare against the gauge.

sampling_plan.reason: captures rain-dominated valley runoff generation and drainage on footslope soils
isolates soil-texture control on partitioning at low elevation under rain-dominated forcing
samples the melt-timing-sensitive transition zone, the strongest control on hydrograph shape
tests soil influence on melt-driven drainage vs surface runoff in the transition band
captures snowmelt-generated runoff from the upper contributing area
isolates soil control on high-elevation melt runoff partitioning

validation_design.observation_source: USGS gauge: American River nr Nile (daily)
validation_design.comparison: aggregated/routed — NOT co-located; requires summing routed runoff from all contributing columns to the gauge point. This capability does not exist in the stack, so NSE cannot currently be computed. As an interim, column-level QOVER+QDRAI seasonal timing can be qualitatively compared to the gauge's seasonal signature (analog/diagnostic only, not NSE).
validation_design.metric: NSE (target, currently unsupported); interim = qualitative seasonal timing comparison

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: baseline 1980-2018 forcing (uniform), native gridded soil per column

requires_capabilities.capability: runoff routing / river routing (e.g. MOSART-style) and contributing-area aggregation
requires_capabilities.why: convert per-column runoff generation into a routed daily discharge at the gauge
requires_capabilities.blocks: computing NSE against the streamflow hydrograph — the primary ask

requires_capabilities.why: impose the elevation climate gradient that drives snow accumulation/melt timing across the 352-1977 m range
requires_capabilities.blocks: resolving the dominant elevation/snow control on hydrograph shape

requires_capabilities.why: verify melt timing that governs the freshet
requires_capabilities.blocks: attributing hydrograph timing to snowpack behavior

requires_capabilities.why: equilibrate soil moisture and snow storage before the evaluation period

requires_capabilities.capability: basin/contributing-area delineation above a gauge point
requires_capabilities.why: define which columns drain to the American River gauge

requires_capabilities.capability: DEM/elevation raster sampling and gridded soil ingest
requires_capabilities.why: expand the stratification rules into concrete elevation-band x soil columns

assumptions: The contributing drainage area above the American River nr Nile gauge lies within the Naches domain bbox and can be delineated.
Dominant soil classes (coarse upland vs finer valley) exist and are separable from the gridded soil raster; specific values not provided in the brief.
The 1980-2018 forcing archive covers the gauge's period of record for any eventual comparison.
Elevation bands (900 m, 1450 m breakpoints) approximate the local rain-snow transition; exact snowline is unverified.
open_questions: Is any runoff-routing capability planned? Without it, NSE at the gauge is unattainable and the request should be rescoped.
What is the drainage area and period of record of the American River gauge, to bound the contributing-area delineation and evaluation window?
Would the user accept an interim deliverable: characterization of runoff-generation heterogeneity and seasonal timing, rather than a routed NSE?
